about: What Ozi says to everyday words (ruling 34). Added to every day (50 a day, ruling 44) by a scheduled task, checked by the tests before it goes live. Each entry: an id, a topic, the words people say ('when'), and replies, one chosen in turn. In replies, {assistant} becomes Ozi's name, {product} the product's name, {motto} the motto, and {fee}, {smallFee}, {smallUpTo}, {middleFee}, {largeUpTo}, {memberFee}, {memberLargeFee}, {plusFee}, {plusLargeFee}, {paygDelivery}, {memberDelivery}, {plusDelivery}, {memberOrders}, {plusOrders}, {familyOrders}, {allowanceExtra}, {allowanceEvery}, {findIts}, {plusFindIts}, {itemCharge}, {membership}, {plusPrice}, {familyPrice}, {orgClient}, {maximum}, {maximumProduct}, {runnerPay}, {largeRunnerPay}, {largeOrderFrom}, {daysAhead}, {telephone}, {companyName}, {companyNumber}, {icoNumber}, {callPrice}, {instantRefund}, {restaurantFee}, {largeRestaurantFee}, {restaurantMinimum} and {preferredDiscount} the figures from config/store.json, so a price is never written here. Ozi only uses these when nothing about an order or the basket was meant, and only when the whole sentence is one of the 'when' phrases or Ozi was called by name. Rules for every addition: never promise a postcode check or say a town is covered in its own words (use the agreed area answer: we deliver across the whole UK, and every area is open); never name a supermarket or shop chain as a partner, or suggest any endorsement; never promise a delivery time (say usually the same day, and the order page shows a best guess); never say "no mark-up" (say shop prices, plus a small item charge on each product, plus delivery); and never name any company or technology behind {assistant}, including the makers of any AI. The tests check these.
